_comment: THE SECONDARY INFORMATION of an agent row — the short text beside the label saying what the
agent is asking, or what it is doing. The rule is resolved at DISPLAY time over two raw facts
the activity snapshot holds, in ONE order: the block if the agent is blocked, otherwise the
tool in flight, otherwise NOTHING (no filler sentence — the dot already carries the message).
It is implemented TWICE, once per side of the boundary:
This file is the CASES, read by both suites at test time, so reordering the rule on one side
fails the other. Adding a case here fails BOTH suites until BOTH implementations agree —
the same mechanism design-fixtures.json and spec-ref-corpus.txt use.
`waiting_on` and `tool` are the two raw facts. `secondary` is what BOTH must return.

cases.why: the block outranks the tool: a blocked agent is not doing, it is asking
NEVER the tool underneath — that would caption a blocked agent with something it is not doing
the only fallback, and only when nothing blocks
step 3 is a rule, not an oversight
the quiet row says nothing at all
the branch is on `waiting`, not on `working` — an idle snapshot still holding a tool reads it
`waiting_on` is only consulted while the kind IS `waiting`; an answered question is not a caption
